title: Proxy Features and Fairness
goals: Explain why removing one field does not guarantee fairness
Propose a contextual review with concrete evidence
vocabulary: A variable that can stand in for another characteristic
An observed association, not proof of cause
A characteristic requiring particular care in a context
A comparison that removes a feature or component

blocks.title: Proxy features and fairness at a glance
blocks.caption: A feature may be legitimate for one purpose and inappropriate for another. Ask what is measured, when it is available, why it predicts and who might be disadvantaged. A correlation alone neither authorizes use nor proves harm. Talk through the intended decision and available alternatives.

blocks.label: Why might removing building but keeping device code leave related information? Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

guided_practice.title: Find a proxy risk
guided_practice.prompt: Why might removing building but keeping device code leave related information?
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Device code is associated with building in the sample and may carry some of that information indirectly.

independent_case.title: Apply independently
independent_case.task: A team removes postcode but retains school code and claims all location-related information is gone. Evaluate the claim and request evidence.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: The claim is unsupported: school code may be associated with location. Review provenance and associations, compare ablations and group errors, and state unresolved proxy risks.

misconceptions: Ask for the relevant counts, units, procedure or saved record. For this week: X occurs 8/10 north and 2/10 south in this sample. This supports an association, not a deterministic identity rule or a causal explanation.

blocks.text: ML MECHANISM
Input → Model → Evidence
Trace the information, fitted behavior, and evaluation proof separately.
QUESTION  Trace suspicious proxies and compare model behavior after a controlled removal.
MODEL IDEA  A feature may indirectly encode sensitive identity or context, creating unjustified differences even when the original field is absent.
PROOF NEEDED  Use an unseen case, visible calculation, error analysis, and a stated limitation.
UNDER THE HOOD  Photo background predicts classroom location and is correlated with camera quality. Model uses background as a shortcut for health labels.
Draw a fresh data → model → prediction → evaluation trace:
A closer explanation

Fictional records show device code X on 8 of 10 north-building examples and 2 of 10 south-building examples. Device and building are associated in this sample. This does not prove device causes model errors or that every X device comes from north. The remaining cases contradict such a universal rule.

Before continuing, underline the decision rule and circle the evidence that supports the conclusion. Explain the example to a partner without replacing the counts or conditions with a stronger claim. Keep the distinction between an observed result and a proposed next step.
Connect the picture and the explanation
Point to the input, the deciding step and the result in this week’s visual. Explain the same step in ordinary words. A picture helps when you can say what each part represents.
EVALUATION DESIGN
Four Tests, Four Kinds of Evidence
A system is not understood until it survives more than one comfortable example.
NORMAL  Expected data and expected behavior.
BOUNDARY  Value close to a threshold, ambiguous label, or uncertain prediction.
MISSING  Necessary field, label, source, or measurement is unavailable.
SHIFTED  New lighting, species, device, subgroup, or time condition.
RELEASE RULE  Passing one case never proves generalization. Predefine expected behavior for all four categories.
